messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: somewhat OT: current world political map in format suitable for map_data()
parts:
The maps in library(maps) date to the 1980s, and in particular the
'world' map is laughably out of date in its depiction of eastern
Europe and central Asia. I can find lots of more up-to-date maps
online (e.g. at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Blank_maps )
but not in any format recognizably related to the format map_data()
expects.

Does anyone know of a source for a _current_ world political map in a
format suitable for map_data(), or a conversion tool? High resolution
is not necessary, this is probably going to be reproduced at no more
than a couple inches square in a paper.

Thanks,
zw

OK, now I have an actual ggplot2 question.

I've been able to figure out how to draw approximately the figure I
want -- using base graphics. The attached MWE 'demo.R' expects to be
run (with Rscript) alongside a directory named "mapdata" containing
two shapefiles from Natural Earth, ne_110m_ocean and
ne_110m_admin_0_boundary_lines_land (the attached 'mapdata.tar.gz'
unpacks into the appropriate set of files) and produces a PDF
'demo.pdf' which is also attached. (If you run it yourself, the black
dots may appear in different locations, but everything else should be
the same.)

I cannot for the life of me figure out how to replicate this figure
using ggplot. map_data() doesn't like the objects produced by
readOGR(), and fortify.sp() gives me nothing but cryptic error
messages (sorry, I don't have a transcript handy). If I understood
how to do that, I feel like I would be on much more solid ground with
map processing.

messages.subject: Re: somewhat OT: current world political map in format suitable for map_data()
parts:
These natural earth maps look great, but I¹m having trouble converting the
administrative shape files. In the example below the
³parks_and_protected_lands² maps is perfect, but the
³admin_1_states_provinces² maps if full of misshapen polygons. What¹s
going on?


library(maptools)
library(ggmap)



area1 <- readShapePoly("ne_10m_admin_1_states_provinces.shp")
area2 <- readShapePoly("ne_10m_parks_and_protected_lands_area.shp")


area1.points <- fortify(area1)
area2.points <- fortify(area2)


US <- get_map(location='Utah', zoom=6)
map1 <- ggmap(US) +
geom_polygon(aes(x = long,y = lat,group = group), data = area1.points)
map2 <- ggmap(US) +
geom_polygon(aes(x = long,y = lat,group = group), data = area2.points)
